What

What Ash Tree Disease Management Involves

Ash tree disease management is the assessment and handling of emerald ash borer (EAB) infestation on your property — a free on-site inspection for exit holes and canopy loss, an honest evaluation of whether trunk-injection treatment can still preserve the tree, and safe removal with chip-drop to our Auburn Township firewood yard when the tree is past saving. Every ash Aaron walks includes a written assessment before you commit to treatment or removal.

The distinction that matters: we don't sell treatment on a tree that's already lost, and we don't push removal on a healthy specimen that's still inside the treatment window. Preventive trunk injection is only cost-effective before significant canopy thinning; once exit holes are visible and thinning exceeds 50%, EAB-killed ash go brittle fast and become a storm hazard. We tell you which side of that line your tree is on.

Why

Four Reasons NE Ohio Homeowners Call Roubic About Ash

The top ash scenarios Aaron walks each month across NE Ohio properties.

Visible EAB Exit Holes

D-shaped exit holes about 1/8-inch wide on the trunk, with serpentine galleries under splitting bark. A clear sign the infestation is active.

Canopy Thinning From the Top Down

EAB thinning starts at the crown and works down. Under 25–30% loss there's still a treatment window; past 50% the tree is done.

Woodpecker & Sucker-Shoot Damage

Woodpeckers stripping bark to feed on larvae, plus epicormic sucker shoots at the base, both point to an ash under EAB stress.

Dead Ash Near the House

EAB-killed ash turn brittle within 18–24 months and shatter in storms rather than topple. Standing dead ash near structures need removal.

Common Ash Questions

Ash Tree Disease Management FAQ

Five things NE Ohio homeowners want to know about EAB and their ash trees.

Can my EAB-affected ash tree be saved?
Possibly — if canopy thinning is under 25–30%, trunk-injection treatment with emamectin benzoate can suppress EAB and preserve the tree. Treatments must continue every 2–3 years indefinitely. Once thinning exceeds 50% and exit holes are visible, the tree is past the treatment window and removal is the right path.
How much does EAB treatment cost?
Trunk-injection treatments run $8–$15 per inch of trunk diameter (DBH) per cycle, recurring every 2–3 years. A 24-inch DBH ash typically costs $192–$360 per cycle. Treatment makes financial sense mostly on high-value specimen ash where the cumulative cost stays below removal-plus-replacement.
Is it dangerous to leave a dead ash standing?
Yes. EAB-killed ash become brittle within 18–24 months of death and fail violently in storms — they shatter rather than topple. Standing dead ash near homes, driveways, walkways, or play areas should be prioritized for removal.
Can I burn EAB-killed ash for firewood?
Yes — once the wood is properly seasoned. Roubic processes EAB-killed ash through our Auburn Township firewood yard, where it's bucked, split, and seasoned 6–12 months. Local burning is compliant; moving the wood across the EAB quarantine line is not.
How widespread is EAB in NE Ohio?
EAB has killed an estimated 90%+ of ash trees across NE Ohio since the 2008–2012 outbreak. Most surviving mature ash in untreated areas are in late-stage decline. The pest is now considered established and ongoing rather than a discrete outbreak event.
